rationale: B is more useful because it gives a clearer concrete recommendation, defines decision KPIs, and adds quantitative thresholds that could guide implementation and evaluation. A has a sensible principle—start simple and add complexity only when accuracy gains justify it—but it stays generic, with no explicit alternative comparison, thresholds, or revisit criteria. B is still incomplete: caveats and revisit triggers are not clearly stated, and comparative reasoning is only partial. But for a careful decision-maker choosing parameter strategy under an accuracy-versus-burden tradeoff, B provides more operationally usable structure than A.
